::: {.rq-lesson}
This check is **not graded and never blocks you**. It asks whether the R skills this game assumes (reading a `dplyr` pipeline, factors, plots, `summary()` tables, missing values) are in place. You will get one of three results: **Ready**, **Nearly ready** (with a brush-up list) or **Not yet** (with pointers to R Foundations). No regression theory is needed.
:::


::: {.rq-test data-test="ready"}

::: {.rq-item data-id="rd-01" data-world="rd" data-type="mcq" data-diff="1" data-tags="r-pipeline" data-hash="oiwuxi.r906pq" data-show="T25lIHJvdzogdGhlIGNvdW50IG9mIGFkdWx0cyBhZ2VkIDUwIG9yIG1vcmUgYW5kIHRoZWlyIG1lYW4gU0JQ" data-explain="ZmlsdGVyKCkga2VlcHMgdGhlIHJvd3MgdGhhdCBtZWV0IHRoZSBjb25kaXRpb24sIHRoZW4gc3VtbWFyaXNlKCkgY29sbGFwc2VzIHRoZW0gdG8gYSBzaW5nbGUgcm93IG9mIHN1bW1hcmllcy4=" data-hints="WyJIb3cgbWFueSByb3dzIGFyZSBsZWZ0IGFmdGVyIHRoZSBzdW1tYXJpc2luZyBzdGVwPyJd"}
```r
ncd |> filter(age >= 50) |> summarise(n = n(), mean_sbp = mean(sbp))
```
What does this pipeline produce?

- One row: the count of adults aged 50 or more and their mean SBP
- A new column called n added to each row of the data in ncd
- One row per person, keeping only adults aged 50 or more in ncd
- The mean SBP of everyone, with an extra column called n added
:::

::: {.rq-item data-id="rd-02" data-world="rd" data-type="mcq" data-diff="1" data-tags="r-pipeline" data-hash="oix86a.r90l76" data-show="VHdvOiBvbmUgbWVhbiBTQlAgZm9yIGVhY2ggc2V4" data-explain="Z3JvdXBfYnkoKSBtYWtlcyBvbmUgZ3JvdXAgcGVyIGxldmVsIGFuZCBzdW1tYXJpc2UoKSByZXR1cm5zIG9uZSByb3cgcGVyIGdyb3VwLg==" data-hints="WyJUaGluayBvZiBvbmUgc3VtbWFyeSBwZXIgZ3JvdXAuIl0="}
```r
ncd |> group_by(sex) |> summarise(mean_sbp = mean(sbp, na.rm = TRUE))
```
How many rows does the result have if sex has two levels?

- One: the overall mean SBP of all adults
- 600: one value for each person
- Two: the counts of women and men
- Two: one mean SBP for each sex
:::

::: {.rq-item data-id="rd-03" data-world="rd" data-type="mcq" data-diff="2" data-tags="factors" data-hash="oixlex.r90zoh" data-show="T25lIGdyb3VwIGlzIHNwZWxsZWQgdHdvIHdheXM7IHJlY29kZSBzbyB0aGVyZSBhcmUgdHdvIGxldmVscw==" data-explain="UiB0cmVhdHMgJ2ZlbWFsZScgYW5kICdGZW1hbGUnIGFzIGRpZmZlcmVudCBsZXZlbHMuIENsZWFuIHRoZSBsYWJlbHMgZmlyc3Qgb3IgdGhlIG1vZGVsIHdpbGwgY3JlYXRlIGEgc3B1cmlvdXMgdGhpcmQgZ3JvdXAu" data-hints="WyJBcmUgJ2ZlbWFsZScgYW5kICdGZW1hbGUnIHRoZSBzYW1lIHN0cmluZyB0byBSPyJd"}
```r
table(ncd$sex)
#> female Female   Male 
#>     14    286    300
```
What is the problem, and what should you do before modelling?

- Nothing: a model treats female and Female as the same level
- One group is spelled two ways; recode so there are two levels
- The data has three sexes; add a third dummy variable
- Males outnumber females, so the sample must be reweighted
:::

```r
ggplot(ncd, aes(x = salt_g, y = sbp)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm")
```
What will you see?

- A histogram of salt intake with the bars filled by SBP
- A scatter of salt against SBP with a fitted straight line
- A bar chart of the mean SBP in each salt-intake category
- A box plot of SBP drawn separately for each person
:::

```r
mean(c(120, 130, NA))
#> [1] NA
```
Why is the result NA, and how would you get the mean of the two observed values?

- The NA is dropped, so the output is simply wrong
- R cannot add numbers stored in a vector; convert it to a list
- The mean needs at least three non-missing values to work
- One value is missing, so the mean is unknown; set na.rm = TRUE
:::

In a model summary the salt row shows Pr(>|t|) = 3.1e-15. How should you read this p-value?

- About 15%: not significant at the 5% level
- About 3.1%: weak evidence against a zero slope
- Not a probability; it is a count of 15 observations
- Extremely small: strong evidence against a zero slope
:::

::: {.rq-item data-id="rd-08" data-world="rd" data-type="mcq" data-diff="3" data-tags="factors,r-pipeline" data-hash="oizfme.r9303a" data-show="VG8gbGFiZWwgdGhlIDAvMSBvdXRjb21lIHNvIHRhYmxlcyBzaG93IHJlYWRhYmxlIG5hbWVz" data-explain="ZmFjdG9yKCkgd2l0aCBsZXZlbHMgYW5kIGxhYmVscyB0dXJucyBjb2RlcyBpbnRvIG5hbWVkIGNhdGVnb3JpZXMuIFRoZSB1bmRlcmx5aW5nIGRhdGEgYXJlIHVuY2hhbmdlZCBhbmQgdGhlIGZpcnN0IGxldmVsIGJlY29tZXMgdGhlIHJlZmVyZW5jZS4=" data-hints="WyJMb29rIGF0IHRoZSBsYWJlbHMgYXJndW1lbnQuIl0="}
```r
ncd |> mutate(htn_f = factor(htn, levels = 0:1, labels = c("No HTN", "HTN")))
```
What is the purpose of this step?

- To make the model treat htn as a continuous measure
- To label the 0/1 outcome so tables show readable names
- To change the values of htn from 0 and 1 to 1 and 2 in the data
- To remove the people with no hypertension from the data
:::
